transitions.use: line of the 220.8-221.8 nm (air) multiplet 3p2 3P - 3s3p3 3D°; flagged 'P' (persistent line) in the NIST Handbook strong-line table

conflicts: 4s 3P° lifetimes: O'Brian & Lawler 1991 laser-induced fluorescence gives 4.5(2) ns for J=0,1,2 (kept); Becker et al. 1980 (LIF) 4.4(4) ns agrees, but beam-foil / phase-shift / older values are longer: Bashkin et al. 1980 5.9(7), Marek & Richter 1973 5.39-5.95, Savage & Lawrence 1966 6.1(8) ns. Smith et al. 1987 normalised their f-values to the Bashkin scale and their own Table 3 lifetimes (e.g. 6.3(6) ns for 4s 3P°, 28-37 ns for 3s3p3 3D°) are therefore systematically long; they are not used here.

3s3p3 3D° lifetimes: measured 22.0(1.1) ns (O'Brian & Lawler) vs MCDHF 26.2-26.3 ns (Pehlivan Rhodin et al. 2024) and 27.8-28.0 ns (Froese Fischer 2005, same CDS table); older measurements 18(3) ns (Savage & Lawrence) and 20.4(1.0) ns (Bashkin, J=3).
221.7 nm line: Lee & Fairbank quote a natural linewidth of 8.8 MHz, whereas the O'Brian & Lawler lifetime 22.0(1.1) ns gives 7.2(4) MHz.
29Si hyperfine A of 3s3p3 3D°3: abstract of Lee & Fairbank (journal and arXiv) -532.9(0.6) MHz; Table 2 of the arXiv version -531.8(0.9) MHz. The abstract value is kept.
29Si A(3P2): -160.1(1.3) MHz (optical, Lee & Fairbank) vs -160.74(73) MHz (laser magnetic resonance, Brown et al., with A(3P1) fixed at an estimate) - consistent.

NIST ASD A-values of the intercombination lines 244.3365 nm and 245.2118 nm (air; 3P1,2 - 4s 1P°1) are reported by Den Hartog et al. 2023 to be in error by +0.32 and -0.53 dex relative to O'Brian & Lawler 1991; the new measured values are 5.52e5 and 5.01e5 s^-1 (9 %).
Highly excited levels where MCDHF and experiment disagree strongly (same CDS table): 3p7s (1/2,1/2)°1 23.6(1.2) ns measured vs 12.17 ns; 3p5d 1P°1 13.4(7) vs 9.83 ns; 3p4d 1D°2 44.5(2.2) vs 36.4 ns.

notes: Level energies are the NIST ASD values (data/nist/Si_I_levels.tsv). Lifetimes of O'Brian & Lawler are quoted at second hand (method 'compilation'). Den Hartog et al. 2023 A-values = their measured branching fractions / O'Brian & Lawler lifetimes, so they are not independent of the lifetimes; the 'branching' field is the measured branching fraction of that decay channel. rme_J_ea0 values are derived from A as described in each note. Isotope shifts are nu(heavier) - nu(28Si) as printed (positive = heavier isotope at higher frequency for the 221.7 nm line). 29Si has I = 1/2 (no quadrupole constant); the 29Si frequency of the 3P1-3P2 interval is the hyperfine-free fine-structure interval. The g_J values of 3P1 and 3P2 are fitted from laser magnetic resonance and carry systematic errors larger than the printed 1-sigma. Lifetimes of 3P1, 3P2, 1D2, 1S0 are derived from calculated A-values (theory), not measured. Additional measured data not transcribed here: Pehlivan Rhodin et al. 2024 Table B.3 (CDS tableb3.dat) gives 17 semi-experimental log(gf) for near-infrared 4s-4p and 3s3p3 3D°-4p lines (measured branching fractions x calculated lifetimes); Smith et al. 1987 give branching fractions / f-values for 108 lines (already the basis of NIST ASD).
